_note: The chemistry grid (scripts/room_chemistry.gd): what each map tile is made of and how materials react. Rules, not special cases: anything flammable catches from a burning neighbour (chance per second = spread), burns for burn_time seconds and ends as ash; `clears` means the thing standing there (bush, crate, fence) burns away and the tile can be walked through. Wet tiles don't catch; `douses` (water) wets its neighbours and stops fire spreading into them. `conductive` is for electricity (not used yet). Tiles not listed are inert (sand, stone, road, rock, walls, the wharf planks: old wet timber).
